procedure_signature.notes: Batch 4J skill 4/5. Owns the CONVENTION itself rather than any computation: the assume-tension convention for structural members (every unknown member force assumed positive in tension, a negative solved value meaning compression); the physical meaning that a member in tension pulls both of its end joints toward each other while a member in compression pushes both of them apart; the fact that the ARROW on a joint free-body diagram REVERSES between a member's two ends while the member's SIGNED VALUE does not change; CROSS-METHOD CONSISTENCY, so the same member reads the same signed value whether reached by joints or by section; and reporting a signed result with a T or C designation rather than a bare magnitude. Boundary: method_of_joints (signed, skill 2) and method_of_sections (signed, skill 3) both USE this convention and both name this skill as its owner; the artifact carries the complement - those skills compute member forces, this one owns the convention they apply, member values are taken as GIVEN, and 'do not recompute' is authored into both the procedure and the prompt rather than left implicit. internal_force_sign_convention (signed, Batch 4H) is the direct beams-family analogue - it owns the N/V/M convention, the equal-and-opposite relationship between the two faces of a cut, and signed rather than bare-magnitude reporting - and this skill is its truss-member counterpart. truss_support_reactions (signed, skill 1) supplies reactions, given not re-derived. zero_force_members (batch sibling, position 5) is excluded with a stated reason: a zero-force member has no sign to assign. Worked example Operator-verified against the same truss analysed by method_of_sections: joints A(0,0) pin, D(4,0), E(8,0), G(12,0) on the bottom chord and B(4,3), F(8,3) on the top; nine members; loads 6 kN down at D and 24 kN down at E; reactions Ax = 0, Ay = 12 kN up, Gy = 18 kN up. Member values given from both signed methods: F_BF = -16, F_DF = -10, F_DE = +24 by method of joints propagating A then B then D, and identically by method of sections cutting BF, DF and DE. Interpretation under the convention: F_BF = -16 kN is 16 kN COMPRESSION, F_DF = -10 kN is 10 kN COMPRESSION, F_DE = +24 kN is 24 kN TENSION. Distinguishing feature bites: compression and tension are both present so the sign carries meaning; ARROW REVERSAL is demonstrated explicitly for one member of each state - for BF the unit direction from B toward F is (1,0) giving a force on B of (-16,0) pushing B AWAY from F, while the unit direction from F toward B is (-1,0) giving a force on F of (+16,0) pushing F AWAY from B, opposite arrows with the signed value -16 at both ends; for DE the force on D is (+24,0) pulling D TOWARD E and the force on E is (-24,0) pulling E TOWARD D, again opposite arrows with the signed value +24 at both ends and both arrows pulling the joints together; cross-method agreement is shown on all three members; and a magnitude-only report is detectably incomplete because 16 kN alone does not distinguish BF, which is in compression, from a tension member of the same magnitude. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane.

procedure_signature.notes: Batch 4F skill 3/5. Scope Operator-derived. The CONTRAST skill to the trusses just signed: a frame or machine contains at least one multi-force member (loaded at more than two points, between its end connections, or by an applied couple), so its pin force is NOT axial — it has two unknown components, unlike a two-force member whose direction two_force_member_identification fixed. This is the FBD and modeling step; solving is frame_machine_equilibrium (skill 4/5), the ceiling, which lists this node as a prerequisite. Synthesis of three signed parents, verified woven: two_force_member_identification (the two-force test, so the multi-force contrast is sharp and a two-force link inside a frame can reduce unknowns), support_reaction_modeling (external reaction components), rigid_body_fbd_2d (how to draw one body's FBD, extended here to dismembered members with pin-interaction forces). The skill owns Newton's third law at each internal pin as a DRAWING rule: the pair on the two adjoining member FBDs is equal and opposite. REVIEW-BEAT CORRECTION, a genuine pedagogy defect not mere wording: the first draft's only internal pin (B) connected multi-force AB to TWO-FORCE BD. Because BD is two-force, the force at B lies along BD — one unknown, not two — and the draft conceded as much in its own solution. The example therefore never demonstrated the two-component pin force that is the entire point of the skill, and it contradicted its own concept (which says a two-force member inside a frame REDUCES unknowns, then drew two components at exactly the reducing pin). Root cause is structural: in any two-member frame with one two-force member the shared pin is always adjacent to it and thus constrained. Redesigned so BOTH members are multi-force — AB vertical with a horizontal load H at midheight, BC horizontal with a downward load P at midspan, joined at internal pin B — so neither is two-force and the pin force at B is a genuine two-component unknown, Operator-verified on disk. 3-signal mapping, all genuinely EARNED and the OPPOSITE of the Decision B count-and-classify debt, because this is the first 4F skill that actually places and resolves forces: axis_confusion at step 4 (mislabeling which of the two rectangular pin components is x versus y — a real error only because the components are now independent, not locked to a member axis), sign_or_placement_error at step 5 (drawing the Newton's-third-law pair with the same sense instead of opposite), unclassified at step 6 (misclassification, incomplete FBD, importing a solve). simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family). Hard stops verified absent: no equilibrium equations solved, no pin/reaction/member magnitude found, no method of joints or sections, no truss determinacy count, no 3D. This lane also recorded a third cross-phase pattern for the Architect: an identification/FBD skill's worked example must EXERCISE the skill's distinguishing feature, not merely include it — the same defect family as contact_force_modeling's single interface and two_force_member_identification's single member, here the constrained pin. Caught and corrected before sign-off.

steps_in_signed_order.application: The between-pin load makes AB multi-force, so the assembly is not a truss.
steps_in_signed_order.signed_instruction: Survey the assembly and classify it: if every member is two-force, it is a truss (simple_truss_modeling owns that case); if at least one member is multi-force — loaded at more than two points, loaded between its end connections, or carrying an applied couple — classify the assembly as a frame or machine and proceed with dismemberment.

steps_in_signed_order.application: Separate the connected members conceptually at the internal pin.
steps_in_signed_order.signed_instruction: For each member, apply the two-force qualification from two_force_member_identification: exactly two loaded points, no intermediate force, no couple, weight neglected or negligible. Label each member two-force or multi-force. For every multi-force member, state that each pin connection force on that member has two unknown components and is not known to act along the member.

steps_in_signed_order.application: Retain two rectangular pin components on the multi-force member.
steps_in_signed_order.signed_instruction: Identify external supports and, taking the support-type catalog as given from support_reaction_modeling, list the reaction components that will appear on the member that carries each support (pin → two force components; frictionless roller → one force perpendicular to the surface; fixed → two force components plus a couple). Do not solve for any reaction value.

steps_in_signed_order.application: Represent the two-force link by one axial line of action while preserving the shared pin relation.
steps_in_signed_order.signed_instruction: Dismember the assembly. For each separated member, draw a free-body diagram showing (i) external loads on that member at their points of application, (ii) support reaction components on that member, and (iii) pin-interaction forces from connected members. On each multi-force member, draw each internal pin force as two unknown rectangular components (for example Bx horizontal and By vertical), not as a single force along the member axis. On each two-force member inside the frame, draw the force along the chord joining its two pins.

steps_in_signed_order.application: The same two pin unknowns appear with opposite senses on adjoining member FBDs.
steps_in_signed_order.signed_instruction: At every internal pin, apply Newton's third law as a drawing rule: the force components member X exerts on member Y must equal in magnitude and opposite in sense the force components Y exerts on X. Check the two FBDs so the paired components are consistent. Do not write equilibrium equations.

steps_in_signed_order.application: Report only the symbolic FBD inventory and stop before equilibrium.
steps_in_signed_order.signed_instruction: Report the frame/machine classification, each member's type (multi-force or two-force), a description of each member FBD (loads, reactions, pin components or axial force), and the third-law pairing at each internal pin. Stop: do not write ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0, or ΣM = 0 to solve; do not solve for any pin, reaction, or member-force magnitude; do not run method of joints or method of sections; do not apply a truss determinacy count; do not go 3D.

verification: The internal pin contributes two shared unknown components, not four independent unknowns.

procedure_signature.notes: Pin action-reaction forces in frame and machine disassembly — a connecting pin exerts ONE pair of equal-and-opposite forces, not two independent forces. The action-reaction relationship is imposed as Newton's third law: with (Bx, By) assumed on member AB at the shared pin, (-Bx, -By) must appear on member BC, equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. THE LOAD-BEARING IDEA IS CORRECTLY DEVELOPED: the two-not-four unknown count is shown as the consequence that matters, since the shared pin introduces the same two unknowns on both member diagrams and thereby couples them, whereas treating the pin forces as four independent unknowns would leave the disassembled system under-determined. The sign relationship is therefore structural, not bookkeeping — it is what makes disassembly solvable. Internal versus external is clean: pin B is internal and exposes the action-reaction pair on separation, while support pins A and C each contribute a single ground reaction, with the precise edge qualifier that a support reaction becomes a pair only if the member is itself separated from the support. LATERAL BOUNDARIES held in one sentence each along the correct pre-solve/solve seam: frame_machine_fbd draws the member diagrams and this skill fixes the relationship between the already-drawn pin forces, while frame_machine_equilibrium solves for numeric values and this skill imposes the action-reaction constraint that must hold before solving — neither re-authored, and no equilibrium solved as the deliverable. Each member diagram is based on rigid_body_fbd_2d, cited not re-authored; the two-force special case is cited to two_force_member_identification, which would fix a member's pin-force direction along its axis, with the general two-component case kept here. The consistency check verifies the pairing independently of any equilibrium: Bx + (-Bx) = 0 and By + (-By) = 0, and the same two symbols appear with opposite signs on the two diagrams rather than four distinct symbols. procedure_signature.notes: Space trusses — three-dimensional joint and member equilibrium, authored to the Architect scope ruling that the distinguishing feature be genuinely three-dimensional and not a re-run of the planar method of joints. Independently re-derived: |r_AD| = sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = sqrt(49) = 7 m, u_AD = (2/7, 3/7, 6/7) with all three components nonzero and normalization (4 + 9 + 36)/49 = 1, so member AD has a genuinely three-dimensional line of action rather than a coordinate-aligned one. The joint solves by THREE scalar equations: from sum Fz, F_AD = 7(7/6) = 49/6 = 8.1667 kN tension; from sum Fy, F_AC = -(49/6)(3/7) = -3.5 kN compression; from sum Fx, F_AB = -(49/6)(2/7) = -7/3 = -2.3333 kN compression. Verified by an independent z-balance, F_AD(6/7) = 49/7 = 7 kN balancing the applied load without reference to the x or y equations, and by sign reading consistent with a downward load putting AD in tension while AB and AC resist. THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE BITES: the third equation carries real work because the member with the only z-component isolates from sum Fz, so the resolution genuinely exercises three-dimensional direction cosines and cannot be a planar problem wearing a z-axis; the artifact states explicitly that a planar two-equation resolution is insufficient and sum Fz is not optional, and states the space-truss determinacy relation m + r = 3j contrasted with the planar m + r = 2j. BOUNDARY against the signed plane-truss family: method_of_joints owns the planar two-equation joint and its complement is named in one sentence; simple_truss_modeling's planar idealization is cited as the analogue with ball-and-socket joints replacing pins and not re-authored; zero_force_members and method_of_sections are excluded; the 3D unit-vector and force-along-line mechanics of unit_vector_along_line and force_directed_along_line are cited and not re-derived. No mass, no dynamics. SYMBOL DISCIPLINE, with one sharp catch: cartesian_vector_components_3d binds k as the +z unit vector, and this artifact uses sum Fz and z-components throughout without ever binding a bare k, avoiding the collision rather than stumbling into it; F_AB, F_AC, F_AD reused tension-positive from method_of_joints, the unit-vector framing reused from unit_vector_along_line, and m, r, j reused as counts from simple_truss_modeling; no binding of d, k, I, M_O, theta, A_gen or V. Three earned signals at distinct steps: sign_or_placement_error at step 2 where each unit vector is formed from the joint outward and the tension-positive convention is set, covering unit-vector reversal and wrong force sense; axis_confusion at step 3 where the three scalar equations are assembled, covering applying only two equations, dropping sum Fz, and Cartesian component mismatch; and unclassified at step 1 as the boundary fallback covering re-running the planar method as the objective and using 2j determinacy. simple_average_used cannot be earned. solution_sequencing_error omitted and argued: solving sum Fz first is convenient algebra on a simultaneous set of three equations all available at once, not a forced phase order stranding a prerequisite — the correct distinction from general_analysis_procedure, where the phases genuinely could not proceed out of order. Honest limitation recorded: the single-joint solution with three unknowns and three equations determines these member forces but does not verify global determinacy or proper constraint, owned by the determinacy and constraint skills; a negative scalar means compression, not an error; and the normalization check confirms u_AD is a unit vector but does not validate the given joint coordinates. procedure_signature.notes: Space trusses — three-dimensional joint and member equilibrium, authored to the Architect scope ruling that the distinguishing feature be genuinely three-dimensional and not a re-run of the planar method of joints. Independently re-derived: |r_AD| = sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = sqrt(49) = 7 m, u_AD = (2/7, 3/7, 6/7) with all three components nonzero and normalization (4 + 9 + 36)/49 = 1, so member AD has a genuinely three-dimensional line of action rather than a coordinate-aligned one. The joint solves by THREE scalar equations: from sum Fz, F_AD = 7(7/6) = 49/6 = 8.1667 kN tension; from sum Fy, F_AC = -(49/6)(3/7) = -3.5 kN compression; from sum Fx, F_AB = -(49/6)(2/7) = -7/3 = -2.3333 kN compression. Verified by an independent z-balance, F_AD(6/7) = 49/7 = 7 kN balancing the applied load without reference to the x or y equations, and by sign reading consistent with a downward load putting AD in tension while AB and AC resist. THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE BITES: the third equation carries real work because the member with the only z-component isolates from sum Fz, so the resolution genuinely exercises three-dimensional direction cosines and cannot be a planar problem wearing a z-axis; the artifact states explicitly that a planar two-equation resolution is insufficient and sum Fz is not optional, and states the space-truss determinacy relation m + r = 3j contrasted with the planar m + r = 2j. BOUNDARY against the signed plane-truss family: method_of_joints owns the planar two-equation joint and its complement is named in one sentence; simple_truss_modeling's planar idealization is cited as the analogue with ball-and-socket joints replacing pins and not re-authored; zero_force_members and method_of_sections are excluded; the 3D unit-vector and force-along-line mechanics of unit_vector_along_line and force_directed_along_line are cited and not re-derived. No mass, no dynamics.
